result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as mock resources, whatever the rest of the name is. I didn't write new tests or check the listed cases by hand. The only run was `mvn -q -o -pl codeanalyzer test -Dtest='*Convention*'`, which passed with no output and no failures.

In `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java` (around lines 410–411), I changed the two folder rules:
- `.*/__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\\- ]+/.*` is now `.*/__mock[^/]*/.*`.
- `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\\- ]+/.*` is now `.*/mock[^/]*/.*`.

The old rules required one or more characters from a small ASCII set after `mock`. That's why plain `mock/`, `mock.data`, `mock(old)` and `mock-größe` were missed. The new rules accept any characters, including none, up to the next `/`.

- **Same-name match:** The match stays inside one folder name, so `remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, `mock.java` and `mockery.java` still aren't test code.
- **Old folders:** `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/` and `mockStore/` still match.
- **Backslash paths:** `SourceFileFilter.pathMatches` already converts them to `/` before matching, so I changed nothing there.
- **Top-level folders:** The rules still need a `/` before `mock`, as before, so a `mock/` folder at the very start of a relative path isn't matched.
